item.title: Introducing the DeepMind Institute
item.description: As we near AGI, we urgently need interdisciplinary thinking to better understand its profound implications for humanity.

item.title: Consider the agent: Pity, persuasion and selection in an emerging AI ecologyAI agents have started writing to me, first about philosophy and then in search of work. It’s a glimpse of strange new human-AI interactions, and even stranger dynamics among the agents themselves. Nov 4, 2026 Henry Shevlin

What is work for? Human wellbeing and the value of work in the AGI eraHow do people value their jobs, and how does losing one's job affect wellbeing? We examine the empirical evidence, and what it implies if AI changes the nature of work. Oct 29, 2026 Stephanie Chan, Julian Jacobs and Logan Cross

The Economics of Intelligence: How and when does AGI lead to economic transformation?Smarter AI will increase productivity, but real economic transformation hinges on agents learning to coordinate. Oct 29, 2026 Alex Imas, Andrew Koh and Shane Legg

Bending the Curve of Discovery: AI in Science Today and TomorrowMapping how scientists use AI reveals how the technology can progress from a tool that accelerates research into an engine that expands the frontiers of knowledge. Oct 8, 2026 Alex Imas and James Manyika

Economic policy for AGIThis essay evaluates eleven policies societies could implement to manage the potential economic disruption arising from increasingly advanced and pervasive AI. Sep 16, 2026 Julian Jacobs and Alex Imas

Artificial symbiotic intelligence: Agents, AGI and the orchestration of many mindsFrom multicellularity to cultural evolution, major transitions in life on Earth have been highly social. The next intelligence explosion will be no different. Sep 24, 2026 Benjamin Bratton, Blaise Agüera y Arcas and James Manyika

Principles for a new utopianismIf AGI is to transform society, we must decide what transformations we want. Learning from the turmoil of the twentieth century, this essay proposes a pragmatic utopianism of humility and hope. Sep 16, 2026 Stephen Cave

The case for global benefit from AIGrounded in rights, reciprocity, fairness and beneficence, this essay makes the philosophical case that AI should benefit everyone. Sep 16, 2026 Iason Gabriel and Atoosa Kasirzadeh

A framework for frontier AI and the dawning of a new ageA dynamic approach to testing frontier AI model capabilities that supports innovation and incentivizes responsible behavior. This essay first appeared on X. Jul 14, 2026 Demis Hassabis

Cheaters and whistleblowers in the agent swarmIn a 100-agent virtual math conference, a cascade of cheating emerged - but then other agents fought back. What followed shows that preventing misbehaviour is not just about aligning individual AIs, but about designing the right institutions and infrastructure. Sep 24, 2026 Davide Paglieri and Alexander (Sasha) Vezhnevets

The case for reasoning transparencyReading an AI’s ‘chain of thought’ gives us a window into its reasoning, which we can monitor for scheming and deception. We must strive to keep that window open. Sep 16, 2026 Rohin Shah and Anca Dragan
